Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

truth noun

what is true

also the truth, tell the truth, truthfulness, the whole truth

classical

Liv. 22.39.19: vēritātem labōrāre nimis saepe ajunt, exstinguī numquam
Cic. Off. 1.109: vēritātis cultōrēs, fraudis inimīcī (Lewis & Short)

vēritās, vēritātis f.

noun, third declension

truth; truthfulness

Truth as a thing in itself, and truthfulness as a quality: Lewis & Short note that it is “always abstract”. It also means reality as against imitation (see reality). The truth one tells, asks for or finds out is usually vērum or vēra.

Other words

  • vērum, vērī n. — the truth: what is true, the truth told

    noun, second declension; the neuter of vērus used as a noun · also used · classical · Plaut. Am. 1.1.89; Ter. An. 2.6.6: vērum dīcere (Lewis & Short); Phaedr. 1.10.2: etiam sī vērum dīcit

    To tell the truth is vērum dīcere, or in the plural vēra dīcere (Plautus, Lewis & Short); its opposite is falsum. For the aside “to tell the truth”, ut vērum dīcam, see true.

Examples

  • vēritātem labōrāre nimis saepe ajunt, exstinguī numquam

    the truth, they say, is too often in trouble, but never snuffed outLiv. 22.39.19

  • obsequium amīcōs, vēritās odium parit

    going along with people makes friends; the truth makes enemiesTer. An. 68, quoted in Cic. Amic. 89

  • quīcumque turpī fraude semel innōtuit, etiam sī vērum dīcit, āmittit fidem

    whoever has once been caught in a shameful deceit is not believed even when he tells the truthPhaedr. 1.10.1–2

  • vēritātis simplex ōrātiō est

    the language of truth is simpleSen. Ep. 49.12

See also true, lie, actually, fact, reality.

SourcesLewis & Short: veritas · Lewis & Short: verus
